It’s our job to stay at the edge of AI. But even at Every, it’s hard to turn our new AI workflows and tools into team-wide habits.

For example, I’ll lovingly clone our editor in chief Kate https://every.?ev_audience=free by taking 30,000 of her historical copyedits and turning them into a skill that lets us edit like her. But getting the skill adopted feels like shouting into a hurricane. Everyone is busy, and there’s no time to try every new skill or tool. What feels like a breakthrough for me ends up turning into one more thing at the bottom of their to-do list.

The best solution for this, we’ve found, is working in the open with a company agent that lives in your Slack. It lets you show instead of tell your coworkers about your discoveries. New AI tools and workflows can spread naturally and virally across your organization.

That’s why we built the Every Agent https://every.?ev_audience=free.

The Every Agent is an AI coworker in Slack that helps you AI-pill your whole company. We built it for ourselves first, to solve situations like mine.

When I cloned Kate, instead of badgering people about my new copyediting skill, I installed it in the agent. Then, whenever we were working on a new piece of writing, I’d post, “@Every, give this draft a Kate Pass.” The agent would leave its suggestions directly in the Google Doc, where my coworkers could see what it did and try it on their own drafts.

Now it’s a standard part of how we work at Every—no explaining required.

For almost six months now, we’ve used the Every Agent to get work done together. It’s become indispensable for keeping our whole team working at the frontier together.

Today, we’re releasing it to you.

The Every Agent https://every.?ev_audience=free has everything you’d expect from a top-tier agentic co-worker: Your whole team can delegate complex tasks in Slack—from pull requests, to marketing plans and finance or data science questions—and expect high-quality work back, done quickly.

But it’s distinctly Every-flavored: It comes pre-loaded with all of the skills and workflows we use to run the company, and is equipped with personalized Frontier Alerts that ping you whenever we publish something on Every that might improve your workflow. We also add zero markup to the tokens you spend on the Agent—what we pay is exactly what you pay.

Best of all, each person on your team gets $15 in free credits to try it. If you want to keep your team working at the frontier, you should install the Every Agent in Slack today:

WHY YOU SHOULD PROMPT IN PUBLIC

Prompting in public works because most AI use is invisible. You do it alone, in a terminal or a chat window. Your coworkers see the finished report or the five new ads, but they never see the request that produced them, or the corrections you made along the way. When you describe it afterward, it sounds like magic, but nobody learns a magic trick without seeing how it’s done.

In a Slack channel, a coworker who would never open a terminal scrolls past the thread and thinks: I could ask for that.

We learned this the slow way. In March we launched Plus One https://every._?ev_audience=free, which gave each person their own agent in Slack. Some fell out of use once the novelty wore off, but a handful stuck around and became workhorses. Colleagues went straight to mine, R2-C2, to report bugs and request features for our AI document editor Proof. Watching those exchanges helped people learn what agents could do—and trust them enough to try it themselves.

After almost a year of experimenting, we’ve found that one shared agent, working in public, AI-pills a company faster than a horde of personal ones. So Plus One is now the Every Agent: a single agent the whole company shares, built with Claude Managed Agents.


HOW THE EVERY AGENT WORKS

You tag @Every in any Slack channel, tell it what needs to get done, and it does the work in the thread. It learns your company as it goes: When something isn’t right, you correct it in the thread, and it can save the correction for next time.

Your Every Agent https://every.?ev_audience=free shows up ready to work:

 * Every’s workflows are built in. The skills we use to run Every come pre-installed, from Compound Engineering to Compound Writing. We add more all the time.
 * It connects to your tools. Connect Google Drive, Gmail, Notion, Figma, GitHub, HubSpot, and more than 1,000 other tools once, then choose which teammates can use each connection. Nobody has to rebuild your setup in their own Claude or Codex account.
 * It comes with Frontier Alerts. Whenever a new model drops, the Every Agent looks through your current tools and workflows and lets you know if the model is worth paying attention to, for you.
 * It helps you spread your best experiments. When a workflow is worth repeating, you ask @Every to save it as a skill. From then on, anyone on the team can run it. The way your best person does something—including every correction they made to get it right—becomes something the whole company can do.
